newsitem.title: USA: Missouri fieldwork slowed by wet weather.
newsitem.headline: Missouri fieldwork slowed by wet weather.

text.p: Wet weather and damp field conditions kept most Missouri farmers from performing significant fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service.
Fieldwork was especially slow in the northern one third of the state but particularly good corn planting progress was made in the southwestern district.
The Missouri wheat crop had not reached the growth stage where a light freeze would be critical and the freezing temperatures a week ago caused little if any damage, the state reporting service said.
The wheat crop was rated nine percent poor, 33 percent fair, 46 percent good and 12 percent excellent, down slightly from a week earlier.
Seventeen percent of the corn crop had been planted, behind the year-ago pace of 40 percent and behind the average planting progress of 21 percent.
Initial planting of the grain sorghum crop was noted with one percent planted, compared with three percent a year ago and three percent average.
Topsoil moisture was one percent short, 65 percent adequate and 34 percent surplus.
